recipes.name: Chef John's Easy Apple Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) package double crust ready-to-use pie crust (such as Pillsbury®
4 large red apples, cored and thinly sliced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in brown sugar, white sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly to dissolve sugar, then remove caramel sauce from heat.

Unroll a pie crust and press into a 9-inch pie dish. Place apples into crust. Unroll second pie crust on a work surface and cut into 8 (1-inch-wide) strips. Arrange strips in a criss-cross pattern over apples or weave into a lattice crust. Crimp bottom crust over ends of lattice strips with your fingers.
Spoon caramel sauce over pie, covering lattice strips; let remaining sauce drizzle over crust and onto filling.

Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and continue baking until crust is golden brown, caramel on top crust is set, and filling is bubbly, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Easy Apple Pie
raw_recipe.description: This apple pie features sliced fruit baked in a glossy, slightly thick caramelized filling for Chef John's unique twist on a popular American dessert.

video.description: In this video, Chef John demonstrates how to make his mouthwatering Caramel Apple Pie. The recipe adds a caramel sauce that's poured over the apples and lattice crust, creating a delicious and intensely flavorful pie. The filling consists of sliced apples, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt. The lattice crust is made with a homemade pie crust, and the butter-sugar mixture is poured on top of the pie. The pie is baked for 15 minutes at 425 degrees F, then reduced to 350 degrees F and baked for an additional 35-40 minutes. The result is a golden-brown crust, bubbling apple filling, and set caramel on top. Whether you're a seasoned baker or a novice, this recipe is sure to impress your guests.

review.reviewBody: I think this is a fantastic Apple pie! I have never used a store bought pie crust but I realise you were only experimenting, and yes you can use any ole apple to make an apple pie, I have tried them all and they all work just fine! I will make this pie again for sure.

This recipe is brilliant! I love how easy and simple this is, and how great it turns out. I bought pre-made dough and it was still delicious, but homemade dough would probably taste even better. I also changed the recipe a little bit: I added 1/4 tsp of cornstarch to the filling to make the pie a little more firm. I also let the pie cool (after baking) for about 5 hours so that the filling could seep into the apples. After the 5 hours I poured a lot of the remaining filling/syrup out of the pie (You could use the syrup/ filling as apple syrup on pancakes or something). This made the pie a little less sweet and a little less soupy. The last thing I did differently was dicing the apples instead of cutting slices. This way the apples soften better, and so that they are easier to eat. I hope you find this review helpful! Thank you so much Chef John!!

Delicious! The first time I made this the apple mixture was too runny. So, I did make the following changes for the second time. I cut up the apples, placed them in a bowl and mixed in 1 tablespoons of lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of flour. I then placed the apple mixture into the pie shell and only added 3/4 of the caramelized sugar sauce. The pie turned out perfect! Not too runny.

It was good. my husband must have his apple pie in a rectangle dish (he likes corners), so I made it in 11x7 pan. I used 5 small McIntosh, 5 small granny smith, and 1 honeycrisp. I used the same liquid as others said it was a bit too much liquid, and it turned out fine. I mixed the liquid caramel ingrediants in a pan with 2 tbsp. cornstarch, then I mixed in the apples as opposed to pouring over the top to make sure they were all covered. I then egg washed the top pie crust. BTW, I needed 3 Pillsbury pie crusts to pull off the rectangle pan. It was good, but I feel it was missing something, might try a diff recipe next time.

I first cooked the apples in a pan with butter just to soften a little. Then I added the sugar and cinnamon. I also added 3 tablespoons of flour, though I like to use cornstarch when available. It works much better to thicken that juice. That's the good stuff. You definitely dont want to just pour it out. Cook the apples with sugar and flour mixture for just a minute until combined. Then I followed the rest and baked. I loved the apple taste coming thru without too much spice. Delicious!

This came together so fast and tasted great! I will never use another recipe. I added about 1 tbsp of flour to the caramel sauce to thicken as he mentioned in the video and a pinch each of nutmeg and allspice. The sauce thickened as the pie cooled but we tilted the pan after taking out slices to spoon the sauce over the ice cream on top. Perfection!
I added the 2 Tbsp of flour but otherwise followed directions precisely. Outstanding flavor and beautiful presentation. Thanks!!

Awesome! I am not in favor of so much sugar, so, we got ripe apples and reduced the white sugar to only a quarter cup, and added one more apple. The recipe is awesome! I made this four times, it always came out great. And when it's cold, it's just as delicious. I used another recipe here of the dough. Really simple, just using flour, salt and butter - the two together make for a very tasty treat. Posted some pics.

Delicious! I only had salted butter so added a bit of sugar to the top. Also I used 5 apples and dusted with flour. Only had one crust so made my own dough for the lattice. Still very easy and delicious! I love chef John! His pecan pie made me famous among family and friends...and as expected this one was just as delicious!

I made this recipe using Honey Crisp and Macintosh apples. I boiled the sauce to get a thick syrup and followed the recipe by using lattice topping and pouring all over the pie. I baked at 425 for 12 min and then 325 for 15 more minutes and my crust is golden with a caramel sheen. Will make again :)
Followed Chef John's advice to add a couple of tbsp of flour to the apples which made it perfect.
Chef John's recipes rock!
Chef John did it again!! Yummy, so easy and moist! John never left me down with his abundant delicious recepices!

Overall I love the recipe and the pie. I used 5 smaller Gala Apples and it was plenty. The only problem I had was the side crust stuck to the sides of the pie pan. Maybe I spooned in the sauce too close to the sides? I read through the reviews and I don’t see any other comments about that. Any helpful suggestions would be appreciated. Other than that it was great. Mine definitely was not watery, I did peel the apples, I will make this again.
Delicious. Big hit at Thanksgiving!
Love this recipe! Used it for a Friendsgiving and plan to for thanksgiving! I used granny smiths and it held together perfectly. Also make sure to grease the pan- I forgot lol
Added some nutmeg and tsp vanilla. Wow!
The only thing that is missing is pour the caramel over the actual apples. I add cinnamon to my apples. I add a 1 tablespoon of all purpose flour to my caramel. It thickens in the pie. Try it
Possibly the best I've ever had. The one change I made was 50/50 Granny Smith and Honeycrisp.
I’m no great cook or baker but this pie never fails to please! I’ve been making it for years now and it’s delicious every time. (AND it’s easy…)
